group.passage: Octopuses are famous for slipping out of aquarium tanks. Below are two short pieces about what such stories tell us: one by a biologist, the other from the blog of a worker at a public aquarium.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: A Biologist’s View
passage_parts.text: Stories of escaping octopuses are fun to share, but they are not the best evidence of a clever mind. Apart from a small beak about the size of a walnut, an octopus has no hard parts at all, so it can pass through any gap only slightly wider than that beak. Slipping out of a tank may therefore say as much about its body as about its brain. The stronger evidence comes from careful research, which suggests that octopuses can plan ahead, solve complex problems, and recognize individual people. The octopus nervous system is unusual, too: of its roughly 500 million nerve cells, more than half are found in the arms rather than the head. Most striking of all, the last shared ancestor of octopuses and animals with backbones lived some 500 to 600 million years ago, so the octopus mind developed along a path of its own. If we want to understand it, we should stop asking how closely it resembles ours.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: From an Aquarium Worker’s Blog
passage_parts.text: Visitors often ask me whether the famous stories are true. In 2016, an octopus named Inky got out of its tank at the National Aquarium of New Zealand, crossed the floor, and slid down a pipe that led to the sea. At the Seattle Aquarium, a giant Pacific octopus named Billye quickly learned to unscrew the lids of jars. So yes, octopuses are clever, and anyone who keeps them learns to cover every tank completely and fasten the lid down. A closed lid is not enough, though. Octopuses are natural explorers, so good keepers give them puzzles and new objects to keep them busy. In 2021, after a review of more than 300 studies, the British government announced that octopuses would be recognized in law as sentient beings, able to feel pain and distress. Most octopuses live only one to three years. For me, that is all the more reason to make those years good ones.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes how the two writers view octopus escapes?

options.A: Text A doubts that escapes prove much, while Text B treats them as signs of cleverness.
options.B: Text A treats escapes as clear proof of a clever mind, while Text B doubts them.
options.C: Both writers see escapes as the best proof that octopuses can plan ahead.
options.D: Both writers blame escapes on keepers who failed to close the tanks.

questions.stem: According to Text A, which of the following is true?

options.A: Most of an octopus’s nerve cells are found in its head.
options.B: An octopus has a few small bones that help it squeeze through gaps.
options.C: Octopus intelligence evolved apart from that of animals with backbones.
options.D: Octopuses and people share an ancestor, so their minds work alike.

questions.stem: Why does the writer of Text B mention Billye?

options.A: To show that octopuses escape more often than most other sea animals.
options.B: To give a second example of an octopus solving a practical task.
options.C: To prove that octopuses can recognize the people who feed them.
options.D: To explain why keepers must keep jars away from octopus tanks.

questions.stem: Which of the following would the writer of Text A most likely say about Inky’s escape?

options.A: It proves that Inky had planned its escape days in advance.
options.B: It shows that octopuses think in much the same way as humans.
options.C: It happened only because the keepers forgot to close the tank.
options.D: It may tell us about Inky’s flexible body, not just its mind.

1.explanation_zh: Text A 一開頭就說逃脫的故事「不是聰明心智的最佳證據」，因為章魚身體柔軟、能鑽過比喙稍大的縫，逃脫可能反映身體多於大腦；Text B 先講 Inky 和 Billye 的故事，接著說「所以沒錯，章魚很聰明」，把逃脫和開瓶當作聰明的表現。兩人的差別是：A 懷疑逃脫能證明多少，B 把它們看成聰明的跡象。
evidence: Stories of escaping octopuses are fun to share, but they are not the best evidence of a clever mind.
Slipping out of a tank may therefore say as much about its body as about its brain.
So yes, octopuses are clever, and anyone who keeps them learns to cover every tank completely and fasten the lid down.

option_notes_zh.B: 把兩篇的立場對調了：懷疑逃脫證據的是 Text A，Text B 則認為這些故事顯示章魚很聰明。
option_notes_zh.C: Text A 明白說逃脫不是最佳證據，「能事先計畫」的證據來自嚴謹的研究；Text B 也沒有說逃脫證明章魚會事先計畫。
option_notes_zh.D: 兩篇都沒有把逃脫歸咎於飼育員；Text B 只說養章魚的人會學到要把水族箱完全蓋好。

B: Stories of escaping octopuses are fun to share, but they are not the best evidence of a clever mind.
So yes, octopuses are clever, and anyone who keeps them learns to cover every tank completely and fasten the lid down.
C: Stories of escaping octopuses are fun to share, but they are not the best evidence of a clever mind.
The stronger evidence comes from careful research, which suggests that octopuses can plan ahead, solve complex problems, and recognize individual people.
D: So yes, octopuses are clever, and anyone who keeps them learns to cover every tank completely and fasten the lid down.

1.strategy_zh: 多文本題先各用一句話寫下兩篇的立場（A：逃脫故事不足以證明聰明；B：逃脫和開瓶顯示章魚聰明），再比對選項；立場對調的選項最容易誤選。
hints: Text A 第一句怎麼評價逃脫的故事？
Text B 講完 Inky 和 Billye 之後，下了什麼結論？
兩人對「逃脫能證明章魚聰明」的看法相同嗎？

2.explanation_zh: Text A 說章魚和有脊椎動物最後的共同祖先生活在大約 5 億到 6 億年前，所以章魚的心智是沿著自己的路發展出來的，也就是和有脊椎動物分開演化。
evidence: Most striking of all, the last shared ancestor of octopuses and animals with backbones lived some 500 to 600 million years ago, so the octopus mind developed along a path of its own.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：約 5 億個神經細胞中，超過一半在腕足，而不是在頭部。
option_notes_zh.B: 與原文相反：文中說章魚除了喙之外沒有任何硬的部位，牠能鑽過窄縫正是因為身體沒有骨頭。
option_notes_zh.D: 近似錯：章魚和有脊椎動物（包括人）確實有共同祖先，但那是 5 億到 6 億年前，作者的結論正好相反，是章魚的心智另走一條路，並且提醒不要再問它有多像我們。

B: Apart from a small beak about the size of a walnut, an octopus has no hard parts at all, so it can pass through any gap only slightly wider than that beak.
D: Most striking of all, the last shared ancestor of octopuses and animals with backbones lived some 500 to 600 million years ago, so the octopus mind developed along a path of its own.
If we want to understand it, we should stop asking how closely it resembles ours.

2.strategy_zh: 細節題常把原文的前半句搬進選項、再換掉結論（有共同祖先 → 所以心智相似）；要讀到原文的 so 之後，確認因果方向。

evidence: In 2016, an octopus named Inky got out of its tank at the National Aquarium of New Zealand, crossed the floor, and slid down a pipe that led to the sea.
At the Seattle Aquarium, a giant Pacific octopus named Billye quickly learned to unscrew the lids of jars.
So yes, octopuses are clever, and anyone who keeps them learns to cover every tank completely and fasten the lid down.

option_notes_zh.A: 文中沒有拿章魚和其他海洋動物比較逃脫的次數，而且 Billye 的例子是開瓶，不是逃脫。
option_notes_zh.C: 細節錯置：「能認出個別的人」是 Text A 提到的研究結果，Text B 提 Billye 是為了說明牠會轉開瓶蓋。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中沒有說要把瓶子遠離水族箱；作者提到要蓋緊的是水族箱的蓋子。

3.strategy_zh: 舉例目的題看例子前後的句子：Inky 和 Billye 兩個例子之後緊接 So yes, octopuses are clever，表示兩個例子都在支持「章魚很聰明」。另一篇的內容不要混進來。

translation_zh.text:
章魚以從水族箱溜走而出名。以下兩篇短文談的是這些故事能告訴我們什麼：一篇出自一位生物學家，另一篇摘自一位公立水族館員工的部落格。
【A　生物學家的看法】章魚逃脫的故事很適合拿來分享，但它們並不是聰明心智的最佳證據。章魚除了一個大約胡桃大小的喙之外，全身沒有任何硬的部位，所以牠能鑽過只比喙稍寬一點的任何縫隙。因此，溜出水族箱這件事，反映章魚身體的程度，可能不亞於反映牠的大腦。比較有力的證據來自嚴謹的研究，這些研究顯示章魚能事先計畫、解決複雜的問題，並認出個別的人。章魚的神經系統也很特別：在大約 5 億個神經細胞中，超過一半位於腕足而不是頭部。最驚人的是，章魚和有脊椎動物最後的共同祖先生活在大約 5 億到 6 億年前，所以章魚的心智是沿著一條自己的路發展出來的。如果我們想了解它，就該停止追問它有多像我們的心智。
【B　水族館員工的部落格】常有遊客問我，那些有名的故事是不是真的。2016 年，一隻名叫 Inky 的章魚離開了牠在紐西蘭國家水族館的水族箱，爬過地板，順著一條通往大海的水管溜走了。在西雅圖水族館，一隻名叫 Billye 的北太平洋巨型章魚很快就學會轉開瓶蓋。所以沒錯，章魚很聰明，養章魚的人都會學到要把每個水族箱完全蓋好、把蓋子固定住。不過，光是蓋好蓋子還不夠。章魚天生愛探索，所以好的飼育員會給牠們益智玩具和新的物品，讓牠們有事可做。2021 年，在一項涵蓋 300 多份研究的評估之後，英國政府宣布將在法律上承認章魚是有感知能力的生物，能感受到痛苦與不適。大多數章魚只能活一到三年。對我來說，這更是讓牠們好好度過這幾年的理由。

open_tasks.prompt: Compare the two writers. For each text, write one English sentence about what the writer thinks octopus escapes show and one piece of evidence the writer gives.

problems: Text A「Apart from a small beak about the size of a walnut, an octopus has no hard parts at all」：事實單 f7 與 Smithsonian（s3）講的是北太平洋巨型章魚，「胡桃大小」是這個大型物種的喙；選文把它寫成所有章魚的一般特徵（只有喙是硬的部位這一點對章魚普遍成立）。屬事實單之外的概括，不影響任何小題（第 2 題 B、第 4 題 D 只需要「沒有骨頭、身體柔軟」），列 warn；改版時可寫成 a giant Pacific octopus 或拿掉 walnut
Text A、Text B 的作者身分（一位生物學家、一位公立水族館員工的部落格）是虛構的寫作框架，文中的事實都對得上事實單；Text B 的「Visitors often ask me」屬虛構情境，不是事實主張，列 warn 供人工審核
details.method_zh: 逐句比對選文、圖表（caption、description、chart 數值）、題幹與選項中的事實與數字和事實單；圖表數值重新下載來源資料比對；可開啟的來源逐條確認（見各條 note）。
